order: Restrict the review warmup to pinned checkouts and sync the docs. A warmup command writes — an engine import is not a read — so running it against a live tree means the review process modifying the user's working tree, which a review must never do. The warmup exists because a fresh checkout lacks the generated artifacts a long-lived tree has, so pinned mode is also the only mode that needs it. Make a live-tree review say so in its preflight instead of silently writing, and name the flag that brings the warmup back. Cover the change with two tests, one showing that the refusal is reported and one showing that the file the warmup would have created does not appear in the project. Update the changelog, the two readme files and the field-validation notes to match, and leave the reviewer's tree-integrity check, its allowlist, its defaults and its reported wording as the base has them.
claims: A live-tree review no longer runs the warmup — the preflight states the refusal and names the flag that restores it, and the warmup now runs inside the throwaway pinned checkout. The changelog, both readme files and the field-validation notes were updated to match. Two new cases in the review-lane suite cover it, one confirming the refusal is reported and one confirming the file the warmup would have created does not appear in the project afterwards. No other behaviour of the runner was touched.
